# qwen-dap-mcp

> Give AI coding agents a real native debugger.

qwen-dap-mcp is an open-source TypeScript bridge from the Debug Adapter Protocol (DAP) to the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It is designed primarily for Qwen Code and exposes structured native-debugger evidence such as stack frames, registers, locals, exception state, modules, disassembly, bounded memory reads, crash dumps, multi-session differential comparisons, and bounded runtime writer traces.

## Canonical links

- Repository: https://github.com/SLP-DEV1/qwen-dap-mcp
- Releases: https://github.com/SLP-DEV1/qwen-dap-mcp/releases
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@slp-dev1/qwen-dap-mcp
- MCP Registry name: io.github.SLP-DEV1/qwen-dap-mcp
- License: Apache-2.0

## Installation

Qwen Code from GitHub:

qwen extensions install SLP-DEV1/qwen-dap-mcp

Qwen Code from npm:

qwen extensions install @slp-dev1/qwen-dap-mcp

Generic local stdio MCP launch:

npx -y @slp-dev1/qwen-dap-mcp

## Core capabilities

- DAP-to-MCP bridge for native debugging
- CodeLLDB, upstream lldb-dap, and GNU GDB DAP workflows
- structured crash, hang, and stop diagnosis
- isolated request-local multi-session debugging
- hardened gdbserver/lldb-server remote attach
- semantic known-good versus failing runtime comparison with `debug_compare_runs`
- ASLR-aware value comparison that separates unstable raw addresses from semantic state changes
- bounded temporal writer timelines with `debug_trace_value`
- request-local operation deadlines, cancellation propagation, and transport-generation isolation
- stack, registers, locals, scopes, modules and exception evidence
- disassembly and bounded memory inspection
- Windows minidump/postmortem analysis
- runtime root-cause backtracking
- crash fingerprints and fix verification
- bounded autonomous diagnose/fix/build/reproduce/verify orchestration

## Safety boundaries

The MCP server is local stdio only. It does not expose a general shell primitive, a general source-writing primitive, or unrestricted memory writes. Live attach and execution-control/value-tracing operations are intended only for authorized targets. Dump sessions are read-only. Optional HOL Guard integration can fail closed before protected adapter starts or mutating/executable DAP actions cross the transport boundary.
